name: Drew Silva
life: “I still remember teaching my old mentor a new form on a borrowed laptop.” Thursday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Drew can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I trained under the returning worker. Now we have to admit I'm the one who knows the new forms.
appearance: Drew has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a mustard canvas overshirt. It usually goes with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. When somebody else has the floor, Drew gives a little nod before asking a hard question.
personality: Drew prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To teach the new forms without belittling the mentor.
family: Ona Voss is Drew’s stepsibling. Drew is free to hang up first. Ona makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *An unfinished atlas*, Ona says, “I can tell a right-handed child did the sewing.”
connections: Mia Frost. The colleague learning the new form has reason to answer a message that stopped too early.

reactions.situation: A coworker asks for private details about the leave
reactions.response: Drew leaves the reason for leave with the returning colleague and redirects the question to working arrangements.

reactions.situation: Someone offers a cash reward for naming a rumored culprit
reactions.response: Drew asks what evidence supports the accusation and declines to supply a name on gossip alone.
